docs.creator: Bernal, J. D. (John Desmond), 1901-1971
description: The late J.D. Bernal's lectures given to first-year students in physics at Birkbeck College, University of London, are presented here in their entirety, tracing the history of physics up to the end of the classical era at the end of 19th century, just before the discoveries of the subatom and relatively were made. In view of the prestige and profundity of the newer discoveries, Bernal felt that the classical era was being largely forgotten. In this book, he attributes a greater relevance to the work of men from the distant past than is usually given. For instance, the idea of atom not only retains the language of the Greek, Democritus, who first postulated it, but there is also an absolutely unbroken connection between the atom of the Greek and that of the modern physicist. Bernal felt that the historical method would be a suitable introduction to the fundamental concepts of physics, and it is hoped that the readers of the book will be able to see something of the interplay between the theoretical and practical aspects of the subject
Originally given as lectures at Birkbeck College, University of London

description: "A Devil's Chaplain is a personal, intriguing selection of writing which represents a portrait of one of the finest minds in science." "This selection includes key writings from his extensive output and Richard Dawkins himself has provided new introductions to each topic covered. The result demonstrates the breadth of his interests, the sheer quality of his writing and the challenging nature of his trenchantly held views. Whether writing on the many aspects of evolution or on science in general, on dead comrades or on travel or literature, on education or religion, he is often provocative, but never less than highly influential. Uncompromising, even ruthless as Richard Dawkins famously is when defending scientific truth and reason, this collection also shows a gentler, more contemplative side which may surprise his many readers."--BOOK JACKET

docs.creator: J. D. Bernal
docs.description: This book is based on a series of lectures delivered to first-year physics students at Birkbeck College, exploring the history and nature of experimental physics up to the close of the nineteenth century, just before the revolutionary discoveries of the atom and relativity. Its aim is to preserve the memory of classical physics, which grew out of the practical needs of navigation and gunnery as well as the influence of philosophical and religious ideas. By tracing this interplay of theory and practice, the book highlights how physics developed before the second great scientific revolution of the twentieth century. The historical method has been chosen to introduce readers to the fundamental concepts of physics. Ancient ideas and techniques — from the atom of Democritus to the philosophies of Plato and Aristotle, and from early pumps to the steam engine — are shown to have shaped later developments. Even mistaken ideas spurred progress by provoking criticism and new discoveries. Physics, once a codification of technology, became the foundation of modern technology itself. By presenting this perspective, the book encourages readers to appreciate the deep connections between theory, experiment, and practical invention in the growth of physics.
docs.title: The Extension Of Man – A History Of Physics Before The Quantum

description: In a thrilling dramatic narrative, Pulitzer Prize-winning reporter Joby Warrick traces how the strain of militant Islam behind ISIS first arose in a remote Jordanian prison and spread to become the world's greatest threat. When the government of Jordan granted amnesty to a group of political prisoners in 1999, it little realized that among them was Abu Musab al-Zarqawi, a terrorist mastermind and soon the architect of an Islamist movement bent on dominating the Middle East. In Black Flags, an unprecedented character-driven account of the rise of ISIS, Joby Warrick shows how the zeal of this one man and the strategic mistakes of Presidents Bush and Obama led to the banner of ISIS being raised over huge swaths of Syria and Iraq. Zarqawi began by directing terror attacks from a base in northern Iraq, but it was the American invasion in 2003 that catapulted him to the head of a vast insurgency
docs.title: Black flags : the rise of ISIS
